architecture_assessment.current_capability: It compiles 17 hand-registered header-format markdown ontologies plus the Aristotle table set into a single 664,494-byte JSON containing 701 concept nodes, 72 Aristotle-only cross-pipeline hooks, 64 tension edges and 1,722 canonical terms, in 0.02 s. Each node is ten flat fields: name, greek, transliteration, translation, definition, type, units, text, aliases, centralityTier. That is the entire runtime payload — concept NAMES, one-paragraph definitions, and a coarse tier label. It carries no provenance at all: the emitted key set contains none of sourceFile/path/line/offset/unit/page/sourceAuthor. It reads only two hardcoded filenames per entry (book-level-ontology.md, cluster-ontology.md at :1221-1223) and ignores the 12 structured *-ontology.json files sitting beside them. Of 482,731 bytes of header-format ontology source, 181,140 (37.5%) never enter the parse loop because they precede the first node marker (:539-540), and a further 153 pipe-table rows lie outside the 3A window the table path scans (:558). Global edge lists, contested-concept sections, tension-summary prose and cross-pipeline concordance tables are outside what it reads. Where it does read them it reads them by accident: 21,879 characters of section 3B/3C/3D/3E content are currently laundered into two nodes' metadata fields by the :718-721 bug.
architecture_assessment.ceiling: Throughput is not the constraint. 0.02 s for 701 nodes means 100x volume (~70,000 nodes) parses in ~2 s and serialises to ~66 MB — the compiler survives that. Four other things break first. (1) CORRECTNESS DOES NOT SCALE: zero validation and zero error signal — no sys.exit, no counter, no --strict, no argparse, and warn() fires 0 times on the current corpus while corrupting two nodes and discarding 37.5% of input. At 100x that is roughly 200 silently corrupt nodes and ~18 MB of silently discarded source, with a clean exit code every time. (2) REGISTRATION DOES NOT SCALE: TEXT_DIRS is a 19-key Python literal; 8 real entry directories are already unregistered and invisible, three with finished ontology files (26,875 bytes). At 100x, entry registration is a code edit per entry with no discovery and no missing-entry error. (3) THE ARTIFACT SHAPE DOES NOT SCALE: one indent=2 JSON blob loaded and parsed in full by the retrieval layer into an uninvalidated module cache. 66 MB is already past comfortable for that pattern. (4) DETERMINISM IS ALREADY BROKEN: five runs produce five different files (101 tie groups, 106 flipped positions) and builtAt is a microsecond timestamp, so the tracked artifact cannot be reviewed by diff at any volume.
architecture_assessment.claim_level_readiness: Nothing in this code is close, and three of the four required changes are rewrites rather than edits. (a) SPANS. A claim record is (text, source_path, heading_path, line_start, line_end, char_start, char_end, type, subject, polarity, evidence_refs); a clause record adds a parent-claim id and an intra-sentence span. The current parsers work on text.splitlines() and re.split() and discard offsets in the first statement of every function (:244, :326, :533, :577, :679, :701) — there is no point in the code where a byte offset is still available. Adding provenance is a parser rewrite, not a schema addition. (b) A REAL GRAMMAR. The state machine at :701-724 is four elif arms over two mutable variables with one dead branch; it cannot distinguish a field from a heading from a table row from prose, which is exactly why 21,879 characters ended up inside a centralityTier. Claim extraction needs at minimum a markdown block parser (headings -> tree, tables -> typed rows, lists -> typed items) before any semantic layer. (c) VOLUME MATH. 224 documents at a conservative ~200 claims each is ~45,000 claim records; at ~2,000 clauses each it is ~450,000 clause records. At ~500 bytes per span-anchored record that is ~225 MB for today's corpus; at the requested 100x it is ~4.5M claims / ~45M clauses, on the order of 22 GB. A single json.dumps(..., indent=2) written at :1384-1387 and JSON.parse'd by the retrieval layer is off by four orders of magnitude — this needs an embedded database (SQLite + FTS5 with a vector sidecar is the repo's existing idiom), incremental per-document compilation keyed on content hash, and a query API instead of a blob. (d) VALIDATION AS A GATE. At claim level, silent corruption is unrecoverable — you cannot eyeball a wrong span in 45M records. Every record needs a schema assertion at write time and the compiler must fail the build.
architecture_assessment.harden_or_replace: REPLACE the parse layer; keep the corpus, the entry conventions, and roughly a hundred lines of glue. The argument is evidential, not aesthetic. First: the structured data already exists. Twelve *-ontology.json files sit in the same directories the compiler scrapes, and Heidegger and Rhetoric's is a 56,912-byte record with canonical_nodes carrying contributors and cross_pipeline_links, plus contested_concepts with per-contributor readings and a tension_summary. The compiler ignores all of it — the string 'ontology.json' appears nowhere in 1,412 lines — and regex-scrapes the markdown twin, where it loses precisely those fields. Hardening a scraper that is competing with a structured file in the same folder is work spent to reach a worse result. Second: the defect density is architectural, not incidental. In a 500-line window I found 2 nodes with corrupted shipped output, 17+ silent-discard branches, 4 pieces of dead or unreachable code, 3 latent silent-row-deletion paths in the table reader, and zero tests. The bugs are not independent — they descend from one decision, to parse a structured document with line-at-a-time regex and mutable flags. Fixing :718-721 fixes 2 nodes; it does not make :539-540, :558, :606, :611-614 or the absent provenance any less true. Third: the goal makes the current schema a dead end. 'Every claim and every clause, every point of connection and every weakness' requires span provenance in the record, and the current record has none and cannot acquire any without a parser that tracks offsets. That said, replacement is not a rewrite from zero and should not be sold as one. Concretely: (1) FIRST, before touching anything, write the golden-file test that does not exist — compile a fixture corpus, assert exact JSON. ~120 lines, and it makes every subsequent step reviewable. (2) Ship the three cheap high-value fixes behind that test: reorder :718-721, add `t` as the final sort key at :1304, and drop or content-hash builtAt at :1375. That kills the two corrupt nodes and makes the artifact diffable — about 6 lines, and it should land this week regardless of the larger decision. (3) Then invert the source of truth: read *-ontology.json where present, treat markdown as rendering, and make a missing JSON an error rather than a fallback. (4) Then build the span-preserving block parser for entries still markdown-only, emitting (source_path, heading_path, line/char span) on every record. (5) Then shard the artifact per entry with a manifest, and only then extend the record schema down to claim and clause. Steps 1-2 are days. Steps 3-5 are on the order of 2-4 weeks and delete more of this file than they preserve — which is the honest definition of replacement.

summary:
I read the whole of scripts/compile-corpus-index.py in the working tree (1,412 lines; HEAD is 1,397, the +15 being the three new TEXT_DIRS entries at :57-71), with exhaustive control-flow tracing of the assigned 500-1000 range, and verified every claim against the live corpus by importing the module read-only and re-running its collectors.

The unreachable-break claim is CONFIRMED and the mechanism is worse than described. At :718-721 the arm `elif current_key and stripped:` precedes `elif stripped.startswith("###") or stripped.startswith("---"): break`, and `current_key` (initialised "" at :698) is never reset once a field is seen — so after the first field the break is dead. Instrumented across all 17 header-format ontologies the break arm fires ZERO times while 108 lines / 21,879 characters are absorbed. Blank lines do not terminate either: for an empty `stripped` all four arms are false. Three corrections to the prior claim: the absorption unit is the split SECTION (bounded by the next `#### N. ` / `**N. ` marker), not the file, so only the last section reaches EOF; only 2 of 17 files are actually affected today (Rickert 17,160 chars, BT 4,627); and the swallowed text does not stay in one field, because `- **X**:` lines inside the absorbed tail RE-OPEN field keys.

The polluted node is corpus/index/compiled-index.json name='Preparatory Rhetoric', text='Rickert - Ambient Rhetoric': centralityTier = 10,009 chars beginning 'peripheral --- ## 3b: global edge list | source | relation |...' (Rickert's entire 40-edge Section 3B list plus the head of 3C), units = 973 tokens including '|' and '|------|----------|----------------|------------|'. Its units come from a 6,883-char polluted `chapters` field via the silent fallback at :753-754. The node is 20,377 bytes — 3.1% of the whole artifact; the next largest node is 1,300 bytes. There is a SECOND polluted node the prior audit missed: 'Temporalität' (Being and Time), centralityTier 247 chars of Section 3C tension prose, units 586 tokens of the Section 3E narrative, and its unit list is wrongly inherited from tension entry T8.

All eight named skip sites verified verbatim (:546 :559 :596 :650 :690 :727 :827 :837), and I found nine more in the same 500-line window — most importantly :539-540, which discards everything before the first node marker: 181,140 of 482,731 header-ontology bytes, 37.5%, including Burke's nine analytic sections (ratio catalog, cross-pipeline anchors, tier map) and 100% of the Uexkull file. Beyond that: :558's `^##\s+3A[.:]` gate leaves 153 pipe-table rows unparsed, including Heidegger and Rhetoric's 33-node table with a Contributors column and its 30-link cross-pipeline concordance; :606 lets any cell containing 'node' eat a data row AND corrupt header_cols (verified to emit a node literally named '8'); :611-614 makes one blank line inside a table delete the following row (verified: Alpha/Beta/Gamma -> Alpha/Gamma); :645's positional fallback is unconditional, unlike its sibling at :425. Dead code confirmed at :606 (the '#' arm cannot fire after replace('#','')), :673 (else-branch unreachable), :686 (no-op rstrip), :528-529 and :589-591 (redundant guards).

Zero warn() lines on the current corpus, against a docstring at :14-15 promising them. Nondeterminism confirmed hard: five processes, five different sha256 hashes, 106 of 1,722 term positions flipping. 259 of 448 'greek' values contain no Greek characters because :735-736 promotes any title parenthetical, and 35 ship as '*Umwelt*' because strip_bold only strips '**'. 13 distinct centralityTier values and 47 distinct type values ship. 8 entry directories are never compiled (3 with finished cluster-ontology.md). 12 structured *-ontology.json files sit beside the markdown and are never read — Heidegger and Rhetoric's is 56,912 bytes carrying exactly the contributors, cross-pipeline links and contested concepts the scrape loses. No test for this compiler exists anywhere in the repo.

Verdict: replace the parse layer. The decisive fact is not the bug count; it is that the compiler is regex-scraping prose to recover structure that already exists as JSON in the same directory, and that the emitted record has no span provenance and no way to acquire one without a parser that tracks byte offsets — which none of these functions do. Ship three small fixes now behind a golden test (reorder :718-721, add `t` as final sort key at :1304, kill the :1375 timestamp), then invert the source of truth to the JSON and build a span-preserving block parser for what remains.

The drafting LLM sees ~6,700 characters of index-derived content per prompt — 1.26% of compiled-index.json's 531,408 bytes — consisting of concept names, 200-char definition prefixes with NO source attribution, and dangling unit-ID pointers into a store that does not exist at runtime (compiled-index.json has exactly four content keys; there is no `units` collection). Measured on a representative on-topic gold-standard prompt: ontologyLines 2,977 chars, hookLines 800, tensionLines 2,915; the full prompt with no chunks is 15,723 chars vs 8,297 without the index blocks, so index content is 47.2% of the prompt while carrying 1.26% of the index. Caps are 12 nodes / 3 hooks / 5 tensions with slice(0,200)/slice(0,150)/slice(0,200)/slice(0,5) truncations; those constants do not scale, so at 100x volume the same ~6,700 chars reach the model while the fraction falls to 0.0126%.

Six CRITICAL defects. (1) Without `--execute`, every corpus and index flag is parsed, validated, and silently discarded — cli.ts:1650-1656 forwards only style/length/format/styleProfileId/model into prepareWriteTask, which builds its prompt at universal-agent.ts:2251-2255 from writing instructions + topic alone. (2) 31 of 72 hooks have an empty targetConcept, and `t.includes('')` is always true (cross-author-utils.ts:474), so getActiveBridges never returns empty; I reproduced a prompt for an off-topic query that reads `**Bridge [hook-de-anima-07]:** Summary Matrix (Aristotle) ↔ ? (Unknown)` followed by `Both authors (Aristotle and Unknown) MUST be cited with direct textual evidence`. (3) The duplicate-bridge filter (builder:725-727) matches `[hookId]` but hookLines render `[sourceText → targetText]`, so it never fires — reproduced double-injection on 4/4 realistic topics. (4) The Source Index is built from all works before the 60,000-char truncation, while the constraints say "ALL citations ONLY from authors listed in the Source Index above" — licensing citation of works whose text was cut. (5) buildSectionConstraints emits 0–3 entries per section but writeRollingContext:1156 indexes it positionally, attaching constraints to the wrong sections. (6) The gauntlet's documented "revise up to 3 times to reach 0.85" never runs: orchestrator:3791 passes `?? 0`.

Beyond those: the index selector is raw substring frequency over ≥4-char whitespace tokens with no stopword filter and no score floor (corpus-index-provider.ts:81-91, :108) — I reproduced 12 ontology nodes, 1 hook, and 3 tensions returned for "supply chain logistics optimization in regional distribution warehouses", including EEG functional connectivity, gaze variance, Rede, and Assemblage. generateViaClaudeCode ignores its maxTokens argument entirely (:1338-1352). estimateTokenBudget excludes every index block and assumes a 200,000-token window against 1M-token models, and its result is discarded. The tension-awareness gate is never called from this pipeline, and where it is called its contrastive-marker check scans the whole document for substrings including "but" and "while". `this.log` does not exist on QualityIntegration (three call sites, one on the revision path) and the resulting TypeError is swallowed into a fabricated qualityScore of 0.5. QuotationFidelityStage returns 1.0 when given no corpus. `RetrievalOptions.collections` is assigned once and never read. All prior claims that touch this scope are CONFIRMED except three PARTIALs, corrected in detail below.

Verdict: harden the pipeline, replace the selector and the string-based transport format. The prompt builder, rolling-context tracker, and staged v2 skeleton are sound and worth keeping; scoreCandidate cannot be tuned into correctness, and passing pre-rendered strings instead of structured records is what makes provenance unattachable and the dedup filter unwritable.

findings.claim: Without --execute, every corpus and index flag is parsed, validated, and then silently discarded. prepareWriteTask() builds the drafting prompt from writing instructions + topic only — zero chunks, zero ontology nodes, zero hooks, zero tensions, zero knowledge units.
findings.failure_scenario: `npx tsx src/god-agent/universal/cli.ts write "..." --json --use-corpus --corpus-chunk-count 20 --corpus-min-relevance 0.70 --whitelist --rolling-context` (no --execute). Exit code 0, JSON returned, builtPrompt contains no corpus text and no index content.
findings.consequence: The entire retrieval + index programme is bypassed with no warning on the documented two-phase path. Drafting done through the Task()-subagent flow is ungrounded, and the result is later scored by the gauntlet as if it had been corpus-grounded.
findings.fix_sketch: Forward the full option set into prepareWriteTask and have it call the same retrieval/prompt-build path as writeV2, or hard-error in cli.ts when a corpus/index flag is present without --execute. ~40 lines plus a shared prompt-assembly function.

findings.claim: 31 of 72 hooks have an empty targetConcept. `t.includes(targetLower)` with targetLower === '' is always true, so those 31 match EVERY topic. getActiveBridges therefore never returns empty, and the prompt emits a MANDATORY block naming author "Unknown", concept "?", and an empty bridge body.
findings.failure_scenario: Any topic whose words do not match a real hook. The drafting LLM receives an imperative to cite an author literally named "Unknown" and to ground a bridge whose text is the empty string.
findings.consequence: Directly manufactures hallucinated attributions — the prompt's strongest imperative ("MUST", "verified, high-confidence") is pointed at a null record, and the JSON provenance reports the bridge as successfully injected.
findings.fix_sketch: Guard matchesTarget/matchesSource on non-empty concept strings; skip hooks whose sourceAuthor or targetAuthor is 'Unknown' or whose bridge text is empty; assert in the builder before emitting the MANDATORY block. ~15 lines, plus a compiler fix so empty targetConcept is never emitted.

findings.claim: The duplicate-bridge filter can never match. hookLines render `[sourceText → targetText]`, never the hook id, so `line.includes('['+mandatoryBridgeId+']')` is always false and the mandatory bridge is injected TWICE whenever it also scores top-3.
findings.evidence: Builder: `const filteredHooks = mandatoryBridgeId ? options.crossPipelineHooks.filter(line => !line.includes(`[${mandatoryBridgeId}]`)) : options.crossPipelineHooks;`. Renderer corpus-index-provider.ts:143 `return `- HOOK [${srcText} → ${tgtText}]: ${src} ↔ ${tgt}${bridgeSnippet} [${hook.tag || 'INTERP-high'}]`;` — no hook.id anywhere. Reproduced on 4/4 realistic topics, e.g. "Aristotle ethos as pistis in the Rhetoric and Heidegger existential reading of ethos in BCAP" → mandatory bridge hook-rhetoric-03, marker `[Aristotle - Rhetoric → BCAP]`; `filter would remove any line containing "[hook-rhetoric-03]"? -> false`; `SAME HOOK ALSO IN hookLines (duplicate injection)? -> true`.
findings.failure_scenario: Any on-topic gold-standard or subsection prompt. The same bridge appears under `## MANDATORY THEORETICAL SYNTHESIS` ("You MUST integrate") and again under `## CROSS-PIPELINE INTERPRETIVE HOOKS` ("do not invent additional bridges").
findings.consequence: Duplicated tokens, and the model reads one connection as two independent corroborating records. The comment at :724 documents an intent the code does not implement.
findings.fix_sketch: Render the hook id into hookLines and keep the filter, or pass structured hook objects through to the builder and dedupe by id. ~10 lines for the patch; the structured-record change is the right fix.

`; break; }`, MAX_CHARS = GOLD_STANDARD_CONFIG.maxCorpusBlockChars = 60000. Constraint at :636 `- ALL citations ONLY from authors listed in the Source Index above`. Trailer at :161 `**Total corpus chunks provided: ${chunkNum - 1} from ${bySource.size} sources**` also reports pre-truncation source count.
findings.failure_scenario: 28 chunks across 12 works totalling 75,000 chars. Works 9-12 appear in the Source Index but their chunk text is truncated away; the model is told it may cite all 12.
findings.consequence: The grounding constraint actively authorises fabrication of page numbers and quotations for the truncated tail — the opposite of its stated purpose.
findings.fix_sketch: Two-pass: determine which sources survive the char budget, then emit the Source Index and the trailer from that set only. ~25 lines.

findings.claim: sectionConstraints is a flat list holding 0–3 entries per section, but writeRollingContext indexes it positionally as one-per-section. Constraints are attached to the wrong sections.
findings.evidence: Producer orchestrator:537-557 `for (let i = 0; i < subsections.length; i++) { ... for (const author of sectionAuthors) { constraints.push(`Section ${i + 1} ("${heading}") names ${author} — include at least 1 citation to ${author} in this section.`); } if (headingLower.includes('interpretation') || headingLower.includes('reading') || headingLower.includes('heidegger')) { constraints.push(`Section ${i + 1} ... at least 2 direct quotations ...`); } }` — up to 3 pushes for one i. Consumer orchestrator:1156 `sectionConstraint: sectionConstraints[i] || undefined,`. Additionally retrieval-stage.ts:486 builds them from `constraintHeadings = hasExplicitHeadings ? subsections : deps.extractRetrievalQueries(topic)` while rolling context iterates `subsections` (= extractSemanticRetrievalQueries output when !hasExplicitHeadings) — two differently-derived, differently-ordered lists.
findings.failure_scenario: Section 1's heading names both Aristotle and Heidegger and contains "reading": three constraints pushed for i=0. Section 2's prompt then receives `Section 1 ("…") should include at least 2 direct quotations from Aristotle/Heidegger` under `**SECTION-SPECIFIC CONSTRAINT:**`.
findings.consequence: Per-section citation requirements land on the wrong section and quote a heading the model is not writing; sections past the first silently lose their real constraint. In the non-explicit-headings case the quoted heading does not exist in the outline at all.
findings.fix_sketch: Return `string[][]` indexed by section and join per section at the call site; align the heading list used for constraints with the outline actually iterated. ~30 lines.

findings.claim: The documented "auto-revise up to 3 times to reach 0.85" never happens. The CLI leaves maxGauntletRevisions undefined and writeV2 coerces it to 0, so validateAndRevise scores once and returns.
findings.evidence: cli.ts:1484-1485 `const maxGauntletRevisionsStr = getFlag(flags, 'max-revisions') as string | undefined; const maxGauntletRevisions = maxGauntletRevisionsStr ? parseInt(maxGauntletRevisionsStr) : undefined;`. orchestrator:3791 `enabled: true, maxRevisions: options.maxGauntletRevisions ?? 0,`. quality-integration.ts:1083 `const maxIterations = options.maxRevisions ?? QualityIntegration.DEFAULT_MAX_REVISIONS;` — the ?? never fires because 0 is passed explicitly; :1089 `while (iteration < maxIterations && !currentResult.passed)` never enters. god-write.md:114-116 "**Max Revisions:** 3 automatic iterations … the system automatically revises up to 3 times to meet the threshold." The command block at god-write.md:27-33 does not pass --max-revisions.
findings.failure_scenario: Run the documented /god-write command. Output scores 0.62. Nothing is revised; the 0.62 draft is returned and the JSON reports `revisionIterations: 0`.
findings.consequence: The advertised quality floor does not exist. Every documented run ships the first draft while users believe a 0.85 gate is enforced.
findings.fix_sketch: Default maxGauntletRevisions to 3 in cli.ts, or add --max-revisions 3 to the documented command and correct the doc. One line either way, but code and doc must be reconciled deliberately.

findings.claim: Index relevance is raw substring frequency over ≥4-char whitespace tokens with no stopword filter, no length normalization, and no minimum score. Any topic — including one with zero conceptual overlap — retrieves a full complement of nodes, hooks, and tensions.
findings.evidence: :108 `const topicTerms = topic.toLowerCase().split(/\s+/).filter(t => t.length >= 4);` (keeps "write", "word", "with", "section", "account", "relation", "conclusion"). :86-88 `const re = new RegExp(t.replace(...), 'gi'); const matches = lower.match(re); if (matches) score += matches.length;`. :118 `.filter(s => s.score > 0).sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score).slice(0, maxNodes)` — the only floor is score > 0. Reproduced: "Write about supply chain logistics optimization in regional distribution warehouses." returned 12 nodes including `**EEG functional connectivity**`, `**Gaze variance and fixation dispersion**`, `**συλλογισμὸς τῶν πρακτῶν**`, `**Rede**`, `**Assemblage**`, plus 1 hook and 3 tensions.
findings.failure_scenario: Any topic. "supply" matched "Yuvaraj et al. (2025) supply the cluster's only…"; "distribution" matched "Spatial distribution of fixations"; "chain" matched "the last in the chain of things".
findings.consequence: The CANONICAL CONCEPT NODES block is presented as "the established canonical names and definitions for key concepts in the corpus… Prefer these definitions over paraphrase" while containing terms from unrelated clusters. On the on-topic run this block is 2,977 chars (~745 tokens), several entries of which are lexical noise.
findings.fix_sketch: Stopword list + a real scorer (BM25 or embedding cosine against the definition) + an absolute score floor + an explicit zero-match path that emits nothing. ~80 lines, or delegate to the existing embedding service.

findings.claim: generateViaClaudeCode accepts a maxTokens option and never passes it to the claude CLI. Every gold-standard, rolling-context, and subsection generation runs at the CLI's default output cap.
findings.evidence: `private async generateViaClaudeCode(prompt: string, options?: { model?: string; systemPrompt?: string; maxTokens?: number; })` … `const args = ['-p', '--no-input']; if (options?.model) args.push('--model', options.model); if (options?.systemPrompt) args.push('--system-prompt', options.systemPrompt); args.push('--allowedTools', ''); args.push(prompt);` — options.maxTokens is never read. Callers: :2187 `maxTokens: GOLD_STANDARD_CONFIG.opusMaxTokens` (16384), :1178 `maxTokens: config.rollingContextMaxTokens` (2048), :3609/:3747 opusMaxTokens.
findings.failure_scenario: A 3,000–3,500-word gold-standard request. The 16,384-token budget is a no-op on the primary path; only the Anthropic-API fallback at :1366→:1386 `max_tokens: options?.maxTokens || 16384` honours it.
findings.consequence: Output length is uncontrolled and differs between the primary path and the fallback path — the same prompt yields different-length drafts depending on whether the claude subprocess succeeded. The 2,048-token per-section cap that the rolling-context word arithmetic at :1059-1064 assumes is never applied.
findings.fix_sketch: Add `if (options?.maxTokens) args.push('--max-tokens', String(options.maxTokens));` after confirming the flag name, or delete the parameter so the asymmetry is visible. 1–3 lines.

findings.claim: Ontology node provenance is parsed and thrown away. `text` (the source work), `type`, `centralityTier`, and `translation` are declared and never rendered — the LLM sees canonical concept names with no attribution.
findings.evidence: Interface :16-27 declares name, greek, transliteration, translation, definition, type, units, text, aliases, centralityTier. Renderer :120-127 `const greekPart = node.greek ? `**${node.greek}**` : `**${node.name}**`; const translitPart = ...; const defPart = node.definition ? `: ${node.definition.slice(0, 200)}` : ''; const unitsPart = node.units?.length ? ` [${node.units.slice(0, 5).join(', ')}]` : ''; return `- ${greekPart}${translitPart}${defPart}${unitsPart}`;` — node.text/type/translation/centralityTier never appear. All 701 nodes carry all ten fields; node[0].text === "Virtual Learning Environments (King–Salvo)", type === "FINDING-STRUCTURE", centralityTier === "core".
findings.failure_scenario: The prompt says "Prefer these definitions over paraphrase" (builder:690-693) then lists definitions with no source, while the citation rules forbid citing anything not in the Source Index.
findings.consequence: The single most valuable field for the stated goal — the link from concept to source document — is dropped at the last hop. The block is simultaneously unciteable and authoritative-sounding.
findings.fix_sketch: Append `(${node.text})` to each line and either render or delete the unused fields. ~5 lines for provenance; the real question is whether those tokens are better spent than on the truncated definition tail.

findings.claim: TensionEdge.dependencyRelation and TensionEdge.conflictRelation — the two fields stating what the tension actually IS — are parsed and never rendered. Only nodeA, nodeB and a 200-char description prefix reach the prompt.
findings.evidence: Interface :41-50 declares id, text, nodeA, nodeB, dependencyRelation, conflictRelation, description, units. Renderer :152-157 `const descSnippet = te.description ? te.description.slice(0, 200) : ''; ... return `- TENSION [${id}]: ${te.nodeA} ↔ ${te.nodeB} — ${descSnippet}${unitsPart}`;`. Data (CT-01): dependencyRelation "Rhetorical energeia presupposes metaphysical sense (activity/aliveness as mode of being)", conflictRelation "Metaphysical sense is abstract and atemporal (priority thesis); rhetorical sense is concrete and perceptual (vividness)" — neither injected; te.text (source work) also dropped. 43 of 64 descriptions exceed 200 chars (max 881).
findings.failure_scenario: CT-01 is injected as `- TENSION [CT-01]: energeia (Met Theta: ontological priority) ↔ energeia (Rhet III.11: rhetorical vividness) — Whether the Rhetoric's energeia is a genuine application … The transfer from ontological priority to aesthetic vividne` — cut mid-word, dependency and conflict structure absent.
findings.consequence: The prompt instructs "Acknowledge and engage them — do not paper over them" (builder:743-745) while withholding the structured statement of the tension. The model can only paraphrase a truncated sentence.
findings.fix_sketch: Render dependencyRelation/conflictRelation as sub-bullets; replace the fixed 200-char cut with a per-block budget. ~15 lines.

findings.claim: Three hard-coded truncation constants (200 / 150 / 200 chars) amputate index content before it reaches the prompt, with no ellipsis and no budget arithmetic behind the numbers.
findings.evidence: :124 `const defPart = node.definition ? `: ${node.definition.slice(0, 200)}` : '';`  :142 `const bridgeSnippet = hook.bridge ? ` — ${hook.bridge.slice(0, 150)}` : '';`  :154 `const descSnippet = te.description ? te.description.slice(0, 200) : '';`. Live index: 462/701 definitions exceed 200 chars (73,011 chars discarded even if all were injected; max 901); 36/72 bridges exceed 150 (max 307); 43/64 tension descriptions exceed 200 (max 881).
findings.failure_scenario: Reproduced: `- **koinōnia**: The political-rhetorical community presupposed by every speech act. Gross at Intro p. 11: 'it is in Aristotle's Rhetoric that Being-with, koinōnia, is given its definitive form.' Struever names alltäg` — cut at "alltäg".
findings.consequence: Truncated content reads as complete. With no marker the model has no signal that a definition was clipped, and will complete the clipped sentence from its own priors.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace the three literals with one per-block budget in gold-standard-config.ts, truncate on a sentence boundary, append '…'. ~20 lines.

findings.claim: Unit IDs are injected as opaque tokens with no lookup table anywhere in the runtime. The prompt carries `[META-01-10, PHYS-01-08, DA-01-04]` but no unit text exists in any structure the drafting path can read.
findings.evidence: :125 `const unitsPart = node.units?.length ? ` [${node.units.slice(0, 5).join(', ')}]` : '';`. CompiledIndex (:52-58) has exactly four content keys, confirmed against the file: `top keys: ['builtAt','ontologyNodes','crossPipelineHooks','tensionEdges','canonicalTerms']`. There is no units collection. 4,059 unit references are emitted across 701 nodes; 120 nodes carry more than 5 units (one carries 973, silently cut to 5).
findings.failure_scenario: The model reads `- **φαντασία** (phantasia): A movement resulting from actual sensation… [DA-03-04, RHET-02-03-06, MEM-01, MA-01]` with no way to know what DA-03-04 says.
findings.consequence: This is precisely the gap between what the code does and what the programme is for: the layer below concept names is referenced but not carried. Today the prompt carries concept NAMES plus dangling unit POINTERS.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a units map to compiled-index.json (id → {text, source, locus}) and a per-node budget for expanding top-k referenced units inline. Compiler + provider + builder, ~150 lines, and a large index-size increase.

findings.claim: The token-budget check measures the wrong thing, against the wrong window, and its result is discarded.
findings.evidence: pipeline-utils.ts:50-52 `const chunkChars = chunks.reduce((sum, c) => sum + (c.content?.length || 0), 0); const totalChars = chunkChars + stylePrompt.length + constraints.length; const inputTokens = Math.ceil(totalChars / 4);` — excludes ontologyLines, hookLines, tensionLines, knowledgeUnits, structuralEdges, the topic, the static constraint boilerplate, the Source Index, and priorSectionsText. :47 `const contextWindow = options.contextWindowTokens ?? 200000;` while the models invoked (claude-opus-4-6 / claude-opus-4-8) have 1M windows. Consumer :3579-3582 `const budget = estimateTokenBudget(...); if (budget.overBudget) { recordWarning(...); }` — suggestedMaxOutput (:55) is never used.
findings.failure_scenario: Measured on a representative gold-standard prompt with zero chunks: real prompt 15,723 chars (~3,931 tok), of which 7,426 chars (47.2%) is index-derived and invisible to the estimator. With 28 chunks at 450 chars the estimator sees ~12,600 chars while the real prompt is ~28,000.
findings.consequence: A systematic under-estimate against a wrong ceiling, feeding a warning nobody acts on. Nothing anywhere trims index blocks to fit a budget — the only budget enforcement in the path is the 60,000-char chunk cap.
findings.fix_sketch: Take the assembled prompt string as input, parameterise the window from the model id, and use suggestedMaxOutput to drive generation. ~30 lines, after the maxTokens plumbing fix.

findings.claim: In rolling-context mode the same ontologyLines/hookLines/tensionLines — scored once against the whole topic — are injected verbatim into every section prompt. No per-section relevance, N× token cost.
findings.evidence: :1146-1148 inside the `for (let i = 0; i < subsections.length; i++)` loop at :1078: `ontologyNodes: ontologyLines, crossPipelineHooks: hookLines, tensionEdges: tensionLines,` — bound once at :1021-1023. Chunks ARE re-selected per section (:1122-1131 sectionSpecific + filteredSharedPool); index content is not.
findings.failure_scenario: A 7-section document. The measured 2,977 / 800 / 2,915-char blocks are each sent 7 times: ~46,900 chars / ~11,700 tokens of pure repetition.
findings.consequence: Cost scales linearly with section count for zero information gain, and section 5 receives concept nodes matched against section 1's vocabulary. Each prompt then contains a section-specific chunk set beside a document-wide index set, an inconsistency the model cannot reconcile.
findings.fix_sketch: Call loadCorpusIndexContext per section with subsections[i] (or heading + topic) as the query. ~10 lines at the call site; the scorer still needs replacing.

findings.claim: validateTensionAwareness and detectUnanchoredEdges are exported and never called from the god-write drafting path. The tension block is injected with a hard instruction and nothing checks compliance.
findings.evidence: Repo-wide grep for call sites yields only icp-orchestrator.ts:819/825 (`const { validateTensionAwareness } = await import(...)`, `const tensionResult = validateTensionAwareness(fullText, topicWords);`) and :906/910 for detectUnanchoredEdges. Inside quality-integration's own validateAndRevise (:967-1216) the only index-adjacent call is `validateEdgeCoherence(content)` at :1008. Neither writeV2 (:3788-3799) nor the legacy path invokes the tension gate.
findings.failure_scenario: A gold-standard run injects `## CONCEPTUAL TENSIONS … Acknowledge and engage them — do not paper over them` (builder:741-746). The model ignores it. Nothing detects this.
findings.consequence: An injection with no corresponding verification. The stated goal includes "every weakness"; the weaknesses are pushed into the prompt and never checked on the way out.
findings.fix_sketch: Wire validateTensionAwareness into validateAndRevise using the same topicWords used for injection. ~20 lines — but the check itself is near-vacuous (next finding).

findings.claim: Where validateTensionAwareness IS called, the check is near-vacuous: it scans the ENTIRE text for ANY of 27 contrastive markers including 'but', 'while', 'yet', 'although'. One occurrence anywhere marks every tension as acknowledged.
findings.evidence: :884-886 `const hasContrastiveMarker = CONTRASTIVE_MARKERS.some(marker => textLower.includes(marker.toLowerCase()));` — textLower is the whole document, with no proximity to the tension's nodes. CONTRASTIVE_MARKERS (:812-820) includes 'yet', 'but', 'although', 'while', 'however'. Substring matching means 'but' also matches inside 'attribute', 'distribute', 'contribution'.
findings.failure_scenario: A 3,000-word academic section containing 'distribution' once. `textLower.includes('but')` is true; every tension whose two core terms appear is scored acknowledged, passed: true, zero unacknowledged.
findings.consequence: The gate can only fail on text containing none of 27 extremely common substrings — effectively never for academic prose. It reports a pass carrying no information.
findings.fix_sketch: Scope the marker search to sentences containing both core terms, use word boundaries, and require the marker between the two mentions. ~40 lines; the honest alternative is an entailment check.

findings.claim: `this.log(...)` does not exist on QualityIntegration. Three call sites throw TypeError at runtime; the one at :1174 sits on the normal revision path.
findings.evidence: `npx tsc --noEmit`: `quality-integration.ts(1119,22): error TS2339: Property 'log' does not exist on type 'QualityIntegration'.` (same at 1126, 1174). Source :1174 `this.log('No significant improvement, stopping revisions');` inside the while loop at :1089, reached whenever `newResult.overallScore <= currentResult.overallScore + 0.02` (:1172). The class runs under tsx (transpile-only) so the type error does not block execution.
findings.failure_scenario: `--max-revisions 3` with a first revision that does not improve by >0.02. TypeError → caught by `catch (error)` at :1203 → `return this.createErrorResult(content, error)` → :1463 `qualityScore: 0.5`.
findings.consequence: The revised content is discarded, the ORIGINAL is returned (:1461 `content, // Return original content`), and a fabricated 0.5 is reported as measured. writeV2:3796-3798 only records a warning, so the run reports success and the 0.5 is indistinguishable from a genuine score.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace the three calls with console.error / the existing logError helper, and make createErrorResult set qualityScore to null. ~6 lines.

findings.claim: With no corpus data the QuotationFidelityStage returns passed=true, score 1.0, and a 'minor' issue. Its 0.15 weight becomes free score. corpusSources is never passed by this pipeline at all.
findings.evidence: quotation-fidelity-stage.ts:97-100 `if (corpusSources.length === 0 && corpusChunks.length === 0) { return this.createBaseResult(true, // Pass if no corpus to check against\n 1.0,` with severity 'minor'. Weight/threshold :58/:61 `readonly weight = 0.15; readonly threshold = 0.90;`. Caller orchestrator:3792 `corpusChunks: corpusChunks.length > 0 ? corpusChunks : undefined,`; quality-integration.ts:994-997 `const gauntletContext = { corpusChunks: options.corpusChunks ?? [], knownAuthors: options.knownAuthors ?? [] };` — no corpusSources key, while the stage reads `context?.corpusSources` at :89.
findings.failure_scenario: Non-whitelist run, or whitelist run returning 0 chunks on the legacy path. The stage that exists to catch fabricated quotations reports 100%.
findings.consequence: A document full of invented quotations scores 1.00 on quotation fidelity. Even in the good case the validator runs with sources=[] , degrading matching to chunk-text only.
findings.fix_sketch: Return a skipped/null score excluded from the weighted mean when there is nothing to validate, and populate corpusSources from corpusConstraint.sources. ~20 lines.

findings.claim: RetrievalOptions.collections is normalized into opts and never read anywhere in retrieveContext. --corpus-collections and the textual_analysis / v2_knowledge_chunks push are inert.
findings.evidence: Grep for `.collections` in smart-retrieval-layer.ts returns exactly one assignment inside retrieveContext (`:194 collections: options.collections || [],`); the other hits (:128, :143, :144, :920, :1019) are ChromaDB URL paths and the collection-id resolver. `opts.collections` never appears after :194. Producer retrieval-stage.ts:190-198 pushes the two Lanham collections and logs `Textual analysis collections added: …` at :197.
findings.failure_scenario: `--corpus-collections "theory,empirical"` per god-write.md:57 parses, propagates through four layers, is logged as applied, and changes nothing — every query hits the single resolved COLLECTION_ID.
findings.consequence: A documented targeting control silently does nothing while the goldLog line asserts it worked. Any collection other than the resolved COLLECTION_ID is unreachable at runtime.
findings.fix_sketch: Implement multi-collection fan-out in semanticSearch (~80 lines) or delete the parameter and the flag (~15 lines across four files).

findings.claim: In the legacy pipeline --use-corpus gets ZERO index injection — the gold-standard branch is gated on whitelistMode only. And --pipeline-version legacy from the CLI is silently coerced to undefined, so the documented deprecation path is unreachable from the CLI.
findings.evidence: orchestrator:1777 `if (options.whitelistMode) {` — the branch containing Step 2c corpus-index loading (:2114-2131). The --use-corpus branch is `} else if (options.useCorpus) {` at :2500, whose body (:2501-2563) retrieves chunks and builds a corpusConstraint but never touches ontologyLines/hookLines/tensionLines. cli.ts:1515 `const pipelineVersion = pipelineVersionFlag === 'v2' ? 'v2' as const : undefined;`; stage-types.ts:22-30's deprecation branch is therefore only reachable via the env var.
findings.failure_scenario: `WRITING_PIPELINE_VERSION=legacy … --execute --use-corpus` injects chunks but no index, with no warning distinguishing it from v2. Conversely `--pipeline-version legacy` is accepted and ignored.
findings.consequence: Two divergent grounding behaviours for the same flag, selectable by an env var, with the CLI's own override for it broken — exactly the kind of divergence that makes an output non-reproducible.
findings.fix_sketch: Delete the legacy branch, or make --pipeline-version legacy actually select legacy and make the legacy branch use effectiveWhitelistMode. ~5 lines for the flag; deleting legacy removes ~700 lines.

findings.claim: A +0.10 canonical-term boost is applied AFTER the cross-encoder rerank and then re-sorts, partially undoing the reranker. 447 of 1,722 canonicalTerms are multi-clause sentences that can never substring-match a query, so the boost is both mis-placed and mostly inert.
findings.evidence: Order in retrieveContext: `:238 const reranked = opts.rerank ? await this.rerankResults(query, diverse) : diverse;` then `:252 // Step 4c: Canonical term reranking boost` … `:279 return { ...chunk, relevanceScore: Math.min(1.0, chunk.relevanceScore + CANONICAL_BOOST) };` … `:283 termBoosted.sort((a, b) => b.relevanceScore - a.relevanceScore);`. types.ts:172-173 documents that relevanceScore holds the rerank score post-rerank. Matching at :265-267 `canonicalTerms.filter(t => t.length >= 4 && queryLower.includes(t.toLowerCase()))`. Data: median term length 16, max 118, 1,062/1,722 contain spaces — e.g. "Debate axis 9: social presence reliably predicts satisfaction/learning ↔ effects inconsistent/assumed-not-demonstrated".
findings.failure_scenario: A cross-encoder ranks chunk A above chunk B by 0.05. B contains the literal string 'phantasia' which is in the query; B gets +0.10 and jumps above A.
findings.consequence: A calibrated reranker score is perturbed by an uncalibrated lexical constant after the fact, and the boost's effect is concentrated on the short generic terms — the worst subset.
findings.fix_sketch: Move the boost before rerank or fold it into the reranker input; separately stop the compiler emitting sentence-length canonicalTerms. ~20 lines here plus a compiler fix.

findings.claim: minSourceDiversity has a hard floor of 3 computed from chunks clearing the 0.25 relevance floor, but the chunk block is emitted from the UNFILTERED list. With no chunk clearing the floor the prompt reads 'You have chunks from 0 different authors. You MUST cite from at least 3 different authors.'
findings.evidence: :567 `const relevantChunks = options.chunks.filter(c => c.relevanceScore >= GOLD_STANDARD_CONFIG.relevanceFloor);` (0.25). :571-572 `const uniqueAuthors = new Set(relevantChunks.map(c => c.metadata.author || 'Unknown')); const minSourceDiversity = Math.min(Math.max(3, Math.floor(uniqueAuthors.size * 0.5)), 8);`. :610 `You have chunks from ${uniqueAuthors.size} different authors. You MUST cite from at least ${minSourceDiversity} different authors.` :658-660 `if (options.chunks.length > 0) { sections.push(buildGoldStandardChunkBlock(options.chunks)); }` — unfiltered.
findings.failure_scenario: 28 chunks all scoring 0.20 — possible because retrieval-stage.ts:202 defaults minRelevance to 0.0 and smart-retrieval-layer.ts:196 bypasses the threshold entirely for author-targeted queries. The prompt shows 28 chunks, asserts 0 authors, demands 3.
findings.consequence: A self-contradictory prompt whose only satisfiable reading is to invent authors. sourceListFormatted (:583-587) is also empty, leaving 'Available sources (ranked by relevance)' blank under a MANDATORY heading.
findings.fix_sketch: Compute uniqueAuthors from the chunks actually injected and clamp minSourceDiversity to that size. ~5 lines.

findings.claim: Keyword-expansion chunks have their real relevance score overwritten with a fabricated constant 0.85, which then drives the prompt's 'ranked by relevance' source list, the 0.25 relevance floor, and rolling-context shared-pool selection.
findings.evidence: `kwChunks.forEach(c => { const id = c.metadata.chunk_id || `${c.metadata.source_id}:${c.metadata.page_start}`; if (!seenIds.has(id)) { c.relevanceScore = 0.85; } });`. Consumers: builder:574-584 sorts workBestScore by it for the ranked source list; :567 filters on it; orchestrator:894 `const sorted = [...chunks].sort((a, b) => (b.relevanceScore ?? 0) - (a.relevanceScore ?? 0));` selects the rolling-context shared pool from it.
findings.failure_scenario: An ontology Greek term is used as a keyword query. Its 3 chunks — retrieved by a bare term, not the topic — are stamped 0.85 and outrank genuinely reranked chunks at 0.7.
findings.consequence: The prompt presents single-token lookups as the most relevant sources, and in rolling context they monopolise the shared pool every section sees.
findings.fix_sketch: Keep the real score and record provenance in metadata (e.g. metadata.retrieval_route = 'keyword-expansion'). ~5 lines.

findings.claim: buildRollingContextSectionPrompt computes uniqueAuthors and never uses it. Rolling-context section prompts therefore state no source-diversity requirement at all, unlike the single-shot prompt.
findings.evidence: :279 `const uniqueAuthors = new Set(options.chunks.map(c => c.metadata.author || 'Unknown'));` — the identifier never appears again in the function (:215-380). The constraint block at :280-299 has Grounding Rules, blacklist, section constraint, and Citation Format, but no equivalent of the single-shot `### Source Diversity (MANDATORY — THIS IS A HARD REQUIREMENT)` at :609-620.
findings.failure_scenario: A --rolling-context run: each section prompt omits any minimum-author instruction; the citation tracker (:350-361) lists 'NOT YET CITED (prioritize these)' but never states a floor.
findings.consequence: The strongest anti-monoculture instruction is absent from the mode built specifically to prevent one author monopolising the draft (orchestrator:3702-3704: 'Bypasses the single-shot block below to prevent retrieval-bias from monopolizing one author').
findings.fix_sketch: Emit the same minSourceDiversity computation and instruction scaled to per-section chunk counts. ~15 lines.

findings.claim: Chunk identity falls back to `${source_id}:${page_start}` with no validation, and metadata is typed `[key: string]: any`. When chunk_id and source_id are both absent the key is 'undefined:12', colliding across every document with a page 12.
findings.evidence: Identical expression at retrieval-stage.ts:226/:303/:343, pipeline-utils.ts:18, and orchestrator:936/:1126/:3678/:3686: `const id = c.metadata.chunk_id || `${c.metadata.source_id}:${c.metadata.page_start}`;`. types.ts:170 `[key: string]: any;` inside the metadata literal type, so a typo or missing ingest field type-checks and yields undefined.
findings.failure_scenario: Two chunks from different works, both page 12, neither carrying chunk_id. Both hash to 'undefined:12'; the second is silently dropped by `if (!seenIds.has(id))`.
findings.consequence: Silent loss of retrieved evidence with no log line. At 100x volume the collision surface for 'undefined:<page>' keys grows quadratically.
findings.fix_sketch: Centralise into a `chunkKey(chunk)` helper that logs and falls back to a content hash when both id fields are missing; remove the index signature from the metadata type. ~20 lines.

findings.claim: corpusIndexContributions.queryExpansions is a hardcoded empty array, permanently reporting zero query expansions even though retrieval-stage performs and logs them.
findings.evidence: :876 `queryExpansions: [], // Placeholder — query-expansion logging deferred to a future enhancement`. Producer retrieval-stage.ts:174-182 `const expansion = expandQueryWithOntology(retrievalQueries[i], compiledIdx.ontologyNodes); if (expansion.semanticTerms.length > 0) { retrievalQueries[i] = `${retrievalQueries[i]} ${expansion.semanticTerms.join(' ')}`; goldLog(`Query expanded: added ${expansion.semanticTerms.join(', ')}`); }` — the data exists and is never returned in RetrievalResult (:558-575).
findings.failure_scenario: Every run. --json output at cli.ts:1617-1622 always shows `queryExpansions: []`.
findings.consequence: The provenance record for the one part of the index that measurably changes retrieval is permanently blank, so there is no way to audit which ontology expansions produced which chunks.
findings.fix_sketch: Add `queryExpansions: Array<{original, added}>` to RetrievalResult and thread it to buildLoggingHooks. ~20 lines.

findings.claim: In rolling-context mode the JSON reports injectedBridges that were never injected. buildLoggingHooks independently re-runs getActiveBridges, but buildRollingContextSectionPrompt contains no bridge-injection code.
findings.evidence: orchestrator:4031-4034 `...(() => { const lh = this.buildLoggingHooks(topic, ontologyLines, hookLines, tensionLines); return { injectedBridges: lh.injectedBridges, corpusIndexContributions: lh.corpusIndexContributions }; })(),` executed unconditionally on the writeV2 return path; buildLoggingHooks:857-867 calls getActiveBridges(extractTopicWords(topic)). buildRollingContextSectionPrompt (:215-380) has no getActiveBridges call and no MANDATORY THEORETICAL SYNTHESIS section — only buildGoldStandardPrompt (:700-720) and buildSubsectionPrompt (:1065-1084) inject a bridge.
findings.failure_scenario: `--rolling-context --whitelist --execute --json` reports `injectedBridges: [{id: 'hook-on-memory-01', ...}]` for a run in which no prompt contained that bridge.
findings.consequence: The provenance record asserts something false about what the model was shown; any audit that trusts injectedBridges to explain the draft is misled.
findings.fix_sketch: Have the prompt builders return what they injected instead of a second independent re-derivation. ~30 lines.

findings.claim: _hooksDerivationDone is a module-global one-shot with no reset, while the underlying loader returns a FRESH parsed object whenever compiled-index.json's mtime changes. After a recompile mid-process, hooks lose sourceAuthor/targetAuthor.
findings.evidence: cross-author-utils.ts:56 `let _hooksDerivationDone = false;` with exactly one other assignment at :351 inside the guard at :342. jsonl-loaders.ts:204-213 `const mtimeMs = statSync(indexPath).mtimeMs; if (_compiledIndexCache && … mtimeMs === mtimeMs) { return _compiledIndexCache.data; } const raw = readFileSync(indexPath, 'utf-8'); const parsed = JSON.parse(raw); _compiledIndexCache = { data: parsed, path: indexPath, mtimeMs }; return parsed;` — a new object graph. Hook key census on disk has no sourceAuthor/targetAuthor field at all, so derivation at :344-349 is the only source.
findings.failure_scenario: A long-lived process (observability daemon, batch loop) calls getCompiledIndex, compile-corpus-index.py rewrites the file, getCompiledIndex is called again. The fresh hooks have sourceAuthor undefined, and builder:712-715 renders `(undefined)` into the MANDATORY block.
findings.consequence: Post-recompile prompts name `undefined` as an author the model MUST cite — the same class of failure as the 'Unknown' bridge but triggered by routine maintenance.
findings.fix_sketch: Key the derivation flag on the cached object identity (WeakSet) or on the mtime rather than a bare boolean. ~8 lines.

findings.claim: CommonJS require() inside an ESM package. It works only because tsx injects a require shim; under plain node on built output it throws ReferenceError, which the surrounding bare catch swallows.
findings.evidence: package.json `"type": "module"`, tsconfig `"module": "NodeNext"`. :749 `const { loadCompiledIndex } = require('../shared/jsonl-loaders.js');` inside `try { … } catch { /* non-fatal */ }` (:748-764); same at :412. Verified empirically: a minimal ESM .ts run through `npx tsx` prints `require OK: function`, so the shim exists only on the tsx path.
findings.failure_scenario: `npm run build && node dist/god-agent/universal/cli.js …`. detectUnanchoredEdges' ontology expansion degrades to `[concept.name]` (:777), so Greek/transliteration/alias variants are never checked and every non-English concept is reported unanchored.
findings.consequence: A latent runtime/build split where the difference is a silent quality-signal degradation rather than a crash.
findings.fix_sketch: Use a static import (the module is already in the dependency graph) or createRequire(import.meta.url). 2 lines.

findings.claim: The project does not typecheck. 157 errors, including 4 in quality-integration.ts and 1 in cli.ts on the write path. Everything runs through tsx (transpile-only), so type errors surface as runtime TypeErrors instead of build failures.
findings.evidence: `npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -c 'error TS'` → 157. In-scope: quality-integration.ts(1119,22)/(1126,22)/(1174,16) TS2339 `Property 'log' does not exist`, quality-integration.ts(1144,11) TS2353 `'targetThreshold' does not exist in type 'RevisionRequest'`, cli.ts(1538,13) TS2353 `'renderBboxOverlays' does not exist`. package.json `"build": "tsc"`; dist/god-agent/universal/quality-integration.js is dated Feb 11, months stale.
findings.failure_scenario: cli.ts:1538 passes renderBboxOverlays into agent.write(), whose inline options type (universal-agent.ts:2707-2740) omits it while the orchestrator declares it at :190 and reads it at :3189/:3945. It survives at runtime by accident of JS object semantics.
findings.consequence: No compile-time contract between the CLI, the agent facade, and the orchestrator. Any option rename silently drops the option instead of failing the build. The 'targetThreshold' error means the revision request carries a field the revision orchestrator never reads.
findings.fix_sketch: Extract one exported WriteOptions type shared by cli.ts, universal-agent.ts, and the orchestrator, then drive tsc to zero. The option-type unification alone is ~60 lines and removes a whole class of silent drops.

findings.claim: Compiler field-boundary corruption reaches the drafting prompt verbatim: markdown labels, embedded tags, and section headings appear inside concept and bridge fields.
findings.evidence: Reproduced hookLines from the live index: `- HOOK [Aristotle - Rhetoric → BCAP]: ἦθος as πίστις (Rhetoric I.2, II.1) ↔ Heidegger's Existential Reading of ἦθος (BCAP) — **Tag**: [INTERP-high]\n**Rhetoric locus**: I.2 (1356a1--13): ethos must be produced by the speech itself, not prior reputation. [INTERP-high]` — the bridge field contains literal markdown labels and the tag is emitted twice (bled into the field, then appended by :143). Also `- HOOK [Aristotle - Physics → BT]: Specific hooks ↔ ? — - **` — sourceConcept is the literal heading 'Specific hooks' and the bridge body starts with a markdown bullet. targetConcept 'B&T temporality [INTERP-high]' carries the tag inline.
findings.failure_scenario: Every prompt containing a Rhetoric→BCAP or Physics→BT hook.
findings.consequence: The prompt presents heading fragments and duplicated tags as verified interpretive concepts. The compiler's field-boundary bug becomes a drafting-quality defect because the provider has no schema validation to reject a concept field that is obviously a heading.
findings.fix_sketch: Validate at load: reject/flag hooks whose concept fields contain markdown markers, are empty, or match a heading pattern; log the rejects. ~30 lines plus the compiler fix.

findings.claim: The truncation notice can be emitted twice in one chunk block — once from the inner chunk loop and once from the outer source loop.
findings.evidence: :151-154 `totalChars += entry.length; if (totalChars > MAX_CHARS) { block += `\n*[Remaining chunks truncated for context budget]*\n`; break; }` (inner), then :158 `if (totalChars > MAX_CHARS) break;` exits the outer loop — but if the next source's header pushes past the cap first, :139-142 emits the same notice again before breaking.
findings.failure_scenario: Budget exhausted exactly at a source boundary.
findings.consequence: Cosmetic duplication, minor token waste, and a slightly confusing signal to the model.
findings.fix_sketch: Hoist the notice out of both loops and emit once after them if truncated. ~6 lines.

findings.claim: `.slice(0, 50)` on the logging arrays is a no-op — upstream caps are 12 / 3 / 5.
findings.evidence: `ontologyNodesUsed: ontologyLines.slice(0, 50), hooksInjected: hookLines.slice(0, 50), tensionEdgesUsed: tensionLines.slice(0, 50),` versus retrieval-stage.ts:470-473 `maxOntologyNodes: 12, maxHooks: 3, maxTensionEdges: 5` (identical at orchestrator:2121).
findings.failure_scenario: None — it never truncates.
findings.consequence: Misleading: reads as a guard against unbounded logging when the real bound is set two layers away. Raising maxOntologyNodes to 100 would silently cap the audit log at 50.
findings.fix_sketch: Delete the slices or make both caps share one constant. 3 lines.

findings.claim: Every generation call pins claude-opus-4-6 while the Anthropic-API fallback defaults to claude-opus-4-8. Model choice is scattered across five literals with a sixth default that disagrees.
findings.evidence: `model: 'claude-opus-4-6'` at :2186, :1177, :1209, :3609, :3747. generateViaAnthropicAPI:1383 `const model = options?.model || 'claude-opus-4-8';` — reached only when options.model is absent, which no caller does. Both IDs are valid current models.
findings.failure_scenario: CLI subprocess ENOENT or timeout (anticipated at :1362-1366: 'The claude CLI subprocess can hang when run inside an existing Claude Code session'). The fallback runs the same prompt with the same pinned 4-6.
findings.consequence: Reproducibility depends on which literal you happen to find. Project memory records the intended model as claude-opus-4-8.
findings.fix_sketch: Move the model id into gold-standard-config.ts and reference it everywhere. ~8 lines.

findings.claim: --enable-endnotes is documented in-code as requiring --use-corpus, with no guard.
findings.evidence: `// Parse endnote options (requires --use-corpus)` directly above `const enableEndnotes = getFlag(flags, 'enable-endnotes') === true;` — no check anywhere that useCorpus or whitelistMode is set.

findings.path_line: src/god-agent/universal/cli.ts:1501-1511 vs the rest of the write path
findings.claim: There is exactly one hard failure in the entire write path — a missing --word-target under --subsection-mode. Every other misconfiguration degrades silently.
findings.evidence: :1503 and :1510 `process.exit(1);`. Compare: DESC failure → `catch { recordWarning(ctx, 'init', 'DESC unavailable'); }` (orchestrator:3488-3490); corpus-index load → `catch (e) { recordWarning(ctx, 'retrieval', `Corpus index loading failed: ${e}`); }` (retrieval-stage:481-483); KU load → `catch (e) { recordWarning(...) }` (:438-440); bridge injection → `catch { /* non-fatal: bridge injection is an enhancement, not a requirement */ }` (builder:720); edge coherence → `catch { // Edge coherence is optional — never block the pipeline }` (quality-integration.ts:1045-1047); bbox → `catch { // Bbox validation is optional }` (:1069-1071); gauntlet → `catch (error) { recordWarning(ctx, 'validation', ...); }` (orchestrator:3796-3798). The one genuine circuit breaker is orchestrator:3556-3561 (0 chunks in whitelist mode → throw).
findings.failure_scenario: compiled-index.json is corrupt. loadCompiledIndex returns null (jsonl-loaders.ts:214-216 `catch { return null; }`), loadCorpusIndexContext returns three empty arrays (:106), the three prompt sections are skipped, the run completes with a normal exit code and a normal-looking draft.
findings.consequence: Total loss of index injection is indistinguishable from a run where the index simply had no matches. No --strict, no error counter, no assertion that the index contributed anything.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a --require-index flag that fails when ontologyLines+hookLines+tensionLines is empty in whitelist mode, mirroring the existing 0-chunk circuit breaker. ~15 lines.

findings.claim: The indexPath parameter is threaded through three public functions and explicitly discarded, so callers cannot point the provider at an alternate index.
findings.evidence: :73-77 `function loadCompiledIndex(indexPath?: string): CompiledIndex | null { // indexPath parameter preserved for API compatibility but ignored — the shared loader always resolves from project root. return loadCompiledIndexShared() as CompiledIndex | null; }`. It also drops the shared loader's projectRoot argument, unlike cross-author-utils.ts:337-338 (`loadCompiledIndexShared(projectRoot)`), so this path is hard-bound to process.cwd().
findings.failure_scenario: Any invocation with a cwd other than the repo root, or any attempt to A/B two index builds.
findings.consequence: Index location is implicitly coupled to process cwd with no override, and the API signature lies about it. Blocks side-by-side evaluation of index revisions.
findings.fix_sketch: Honour the parameter, or change the shared loader to accept a full path. ~10 lines.

findings.claim: Two independent, mutually inconsistent hook-selection algorithms run over the same 72 hooks in the same prompt build, with different tokenizers, different fields, different thresholds, and different caps.
findings.evidence: Path A (hookLines): provider:108 tokenizes `topic.toLowerCase().split(/\s+/).filter(t => t.length >= 4)` (punctuation retained), :131-133 searches sourceConcept/targetConcept/bridge/title, :135 `.slice(0, maxHooks)` = 3, scoring is match-count. Path B (mandatory bridge): cross-author-utils.ts:608-613 `text.split(/\s+/).map(w => w.replace(/[^a-zA-ZÀ-ÿα-ωΑ-Ω\-]/g, '')).filter(w => w.length >= 4)` (punctuation stripped), :460-462 re-filters to >= 5, :469-474 matches sourceConcept/targetConcept only, :498 `.slice(0, 1)`, scoring is the 0/1/2 additive scheme at :418-436 with tag and localeCompare tie-breaks.
findings.failure_scenario: Both run on every gold-standard and subsection prompt (builder:702-704 plus hookLines from retrieval-stage:476) and select overlapping-but-different sets — see the duplicate-injection finding.
findings.consequence: Two answers to 'which hooks matter for this topic' in one prompt, neither reconcilable to the other; tuning one leaves the other stale.
findings.fix_sketch: One scoring function, one tokenizer, one cap, called once and split into 'mandatory' (top 1) and 'additional' (next N). ~50 lines net removal.

findings.claim: QualityGauntlet has 10 default stages. Its own docstring is correct, but six other files describe a 7-stage gauntlet and the skill doc lists 9.
findings.evidence: quality-gauntlet.ts:562 `* Stages (10 total):` and :577-588 enumerate ten `new …()` calls. Stale comments: cli/quality/index.ts:17 and :194, quality-gauntlet.ts:458, style-consistency-validator.ts:141, citation-density-checker.ts:62, factual-accuracy-auditor.ts:133, citation-completeness-verifier.ts:174, argument-coherence-checker.ts:355. .claude/commands/god-write.md:100-108 lists 9 (omits ProseAnalysisValidator).
findings.failure_scenario: Weights sum to ~1.20 (documented at :574) and are normalized at runtime; anyone tuning a weight against a '7-stage' comment computes against the wrong denominator.
findings.consequence: Documentation drift across three layers on the component that gates output quality. validateWeights (:618-627) only console.warns.
findings.fix_sketch: Sweep the six stale comments and the skill doc; derive the count from the stage list. ~10 lines plus doc edits.

findings.claim: Every scoring pass materializes and sorts the full node/hook/tension arrays on every call, and the whole 531KB index is JSON.parsed into memory on every mtime change.
findings.evidence: :112-118 `const scoredNodes = index.ontologyNodes.map(node => { const searchText = [node.name, node.greek, node.transliteration, node.definition, ...(node.aliases || [])].filter(Boolean).join(' '); return { node, score: scoreCandidate(topicTerms, searchText) }; }).filter(...).sort(...).slice(0, maxNodes);` — one joined string per node per call, and scoreCandidate (:85-88) compiles one RegExp per topic term per node. 27 topic terms x 701 nodes = 18,927 RegExp constructions plus 701 joins per invocation. jsonl-loaders.ts:210-211 `const raw = readFileSync(indexPath, 'utf-8'); const parsed = JSON.parse(raw);` — whole file, no streaming.
findings.failure_scenario: At 100x (70,100 nodes, 7,200 hooks, 6,400 tensions, ~53MB) a single loadCorpusIndexContext call performs ~1.9M RegExp compilations and 70k string joins, and the loader parses 53MB into one object graph held for the process lifetime.
findings.consequence: O(nodes x topicTerms) per call with no index structure, invoked once per write in single-shot and once per section in rolling context. This is the hard scalability ceiling of the current design.
findings.fix_sketch: Precompute searchText and an inverted term→node index at load time; compile the topic-term regexes once per call rather than once per node. ~10x improvement; beyond that the substring scorer must be replaced by a real retrieval index.
