architecture_assessment.current_capability:
Measured, not estimated. The read path can take a topic string, do case-insensitive substring matching over 701 ontology node names/definitions, 72 hooks and 64 tension records held entirely in memory, and emit at most 12 + 3 + 5 pre-rendered markdown lines into a prompt. For the topic 'The phenomenology of boredom in VR pedagogy and attunement' that is 5,271 characters out of a 656,755-character index — 0.803%. Of the ten fields each ontology node carries, four reach a prompt (name-or-greek, transliteration, definition truncated at 200 chars, first 5 unit IDs); translation, type, text, aliases and centralityTier are never rendered by any code path. Of the eight fields each tension carries, five reach a prompt; dependencyRelation and conflictRelation — the analytic content — are neither searched nor rendered. It is, precisely as the brief suspected, a concept-name carrier. It carries no claims, no clauses, no character offsets, no page locators, no document IDs, and no scores. loadCorpusIndexContext returns three arrays of formatted strings (corpus-index-provider.ts:159); by the time data crosses the module boundary it has already been flattened into prose and every structural handle is gone.

Worse, on this corpus it does not reliably do even that. getActiveBridges — the function behind the 'MANDATORY THEORETICAL SYNTHESIS' block — returns hook-de-anima-07 for essentially any input, including the nonsense words ['zzzzz','qqqqqq'], because 31 of 72 hooks have an empty targetConcept and `t.includes('')` is always true (cross-author-utils.ts:474). That hook has empty targetText, targetConcept, bridge and relevance, so the prompt instructs the model to cite an author named 'Unknown'. The corpus catalog injected into decomposition prompts lists 117 of 578 titles under the header 'only suggest from this list' and mislabels 71 of those 117 as SECONDARY SCHOLARSHIP — including Heidegger's *The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics* and the Greek critical editions of De Anima, Physica and Ars Rhetorica.
architecture_assessment.ceiling: Four separate walls, in the order they are hit. (1) The caps bind NOW, at 1x. maxOntologyNodes 12 / maxHooks 3 / maxTensions 5 (corpus-index-provider.ts:101-103), 1 bridge (:498), 3 tensions (:542) are absolute integers, not proportions. Measured discard on a real topic: 67 nodes scored above zero, 12 emitted, 55 dropped with no count and no log. At 100x volume the emitted context is byte-for-byte the same size while the discard rate goes from ~82% to ~99.8%. The system does not get slower as the corpus grows; it gets proportionally blinder, silently. (2) readFileSync into a single JS string. Node v22.22.0 MAX_STRING_LENGTH is 536,870,888. god-reason/reasoning.jsonl is 21,498,945 bytes today, so the hard throw is at 24.97x — not 100x. At jsonl-loaders.ts:89 that RangeError is UNCAUGHT (process death); the identical read at :210 is inside the bare catch at :215 (silent null, total index blackout). Two different undiagnosable failures from one cause. (3) buildCorpusCatalog is the one component that DOES scale linearly, and that is the problem: 8,439 chars / ~2,110 tokens for 117 titles today, so ~844 KB / ~211,000 tokens at 100x, injected uncapped into every decomposition prompt (llm-decomposition-provider.ts:102-103). Blows any context window at roughly 90x. (4) CPU is the least of it but is real: I timed loadCorpusIndexContext's node scan at 1.94 ms for 701 nodes, extrapolating to ~194 ms per call at 70,100 nodes — synchronous, on the main thread, constructing a fresh RegExp per (term, node) pair. getActiveBridges goes 0.126 ms -> 6.52 ms from 72 to 7,200 hooks, called once per facet. checkSingleTitle goes 0.001 ms -> 0.275 ms from 6 to 6,000 titles per author, called per citation per sub-title, re-running two regex replaces over every title on every call even though the normalized form is already stored as a Map key at cross-author-utils.ts:139.
architecture_assessment.claim_level_readiness: Nothing in these 1,126 lines can carry a claim record, and the gap is structural rather than a matter of volume. Seven things would have to change. (1) A record type. Today the unit of transfer is a formatted markdown string (corpus-index-provider.ts:126, :143, :156). A claim record needs a stable ID, the claim text, a document ID, a locator (page/Bekker/section), character offsets into the source, a confidence, and links to supporting and contradicting records. None of those survive the current renderers, and `builtAt` — the only provenance field in the whole index — is read by zero code, so there is not even a way to say which build a draft came from. (2) A real retrieval primitive. Substring containment over a lowercased `nodeA + nodeB + description` concatenation (cross-author-utils.ts:525) cannot address a clause. At 70,100 nodes and, say, 2 million claims, an O(n) regex scan per query is not merely slow, it is the wrong shape — this needs the inverted index or the embedding index the project already runs (ChromaDB, gte-Qwen2 at 1536 dims) rather than a hand-rolled scan. Note the ontology already carries `greek`, `transliteration` and `aliases` for 448/170/135 nodes respectively and the matcher consults none of them at the bridge layer, which is why 50 of 72 Greek-source hooks are unreachable from Latin-script topic words. (3) Budgeted selection. Replace fixed record counts with a token budget plus a score threshold, and log emitted-vs-scored. Today the cap silently drops the 55 and reports the 12. (4) Validation at the parse boundary. `JSON.parse` into `any` (jsonl-loaders.ts:198, :211) with zero schema, while the file's own docstring at :6 promises Zod. A ten-line schema requiring non-empty concept fields would have converted six of the CRITICAL findings in this report into startup warnings. (5) Streaming readers. NDJSON via readline instead of readFileSync + split, which also removes the 25x wall and the 150 ms main-thread block that becomes 3.75 s. (6) One cache authority, no derived one-shot flags. Three caches over one file (jsonl-loaders.ts:191, smart-retrieval-layer.ts:795, plus the derivation flag at cross-author-utils.ts:56), keyed on float mtime with no size or hash, handing out live mutable references that one consumer already writes into. (7) No truncation-by-slice. `definition.slice(0, 200)` discards 37.2% of all definition text mid-word; `units.slice(0, 5)` discards 2,259 of 4,059 provenance links. For 'every claim and every clause' the answer is a summarizer or a budget, never a character count.
architecture_assessment.harden_or_replace:
Split the verdict, because the three files are not one thing.

KEEP AND HARDEN the loader/cache layer — jsonl-loaders.ts in full (310 lines) and loadManifestCanonicals (cross-author-utils.ts:77-173). This is genuinely good code. The mtime-cache pattern is right, the Zod boundary for KUs and edges is right (types.ts:93-133 even reports per-record failures with the offending field paths), and the dropped-line counters at :66-68 and :103-105 are exactly the observability the rest of the system lacks. Its defects are mechanical and small: a missing `path` field at :224, a bare catch at :215, a `path`/`size` cache key, and streaming reads. Call it 150 lines of change. The one thing to move INTO this layer is schema validation for compiled-index.json, because the loader is the only chokepoint all three consumers pass through.

REPLACE the matching and rendering layer — getActiveBridges, getActiveTensions, expandQueryWithCanonicalTerms, computeMatchScore, extractTopicWords (cross-author-utils.ts:408-614) and all of corpus-index-provider.ts's scoring and rendering (:79-197). Roughly 600 lines. Hardening these is a trap. Every individual bug has a two-to-six-line fix — guard the empty string at :474, fix `.includes('medium')` at :489, add the `u` flag at corpus-index-provider.ts:179, align the >=4/>=5 thresholds — and you could land all of them in an afternoon and still have a system that carries 0.803% of its index into a prompt as untraceable markdown prose. The bugs are not the problem; the semantics are. Substring containment over lowercased concatenations, absolute record caps, and string-typed output are the architecture, and none of the three survives contact with claim-level records.

Two arguments settle it. First, the empty-string always-match at :474 means the bridge feature has never actually worked on this corpus — there is no working behaviour to preserve, only the appearance of one. Second, `grep -rln` over tests/ finds ZERO tests referencing any of the three modules; the sole check is scripts/verify-hardening.ts, which is in neither CI nor package.json and whose one bridge assertion passes only because its test query contains the literal German word 'Erschlossenheit' that happens to sit in a targetConcept. Nothing depends on current behaviour being stable. That is damning as coverage and liberating as a rewrite constraint — the replacement cost is close to the hardening cost, and only one of the two gets you a system that can hold a claim.

So: foundation in the loaders, obstacle in the matchers. Harden ~450 lines, replace ~600, and write the tests first — every CRITICAL in this report is expressible as a property (an off-topic facet must return zero bridges; no emitted hook may have an empty concept field; derivation must survive a cache invalidation; emitted-vs-scored must be logged) and not one of them is currently asserted anywhere.

summary:
I read all 1,126 lines of the three scope files plus ~630 lines of call sites, and verified every claim against the live compiled-index.json, manifest.jsonl, knowledge.jsonl and reasoning.jsonl rather than reasoning from the source alone. All three files are clean vs HEAD, so no dirty-tree line-number skew applies to my scope; the counts match exactly (310/202/614).

The headline is not the cache bug the prior audit flagged. It is that `getActiveBridges` is effectively a constant function. 31 of 72 hooks have `targetConcept: ""`, and cross-author-utils.ts:474 evaluates `t.includes(targetLower)` — which is unconditionally true for an empty string — so those 31 fire for every facet. I simulated the exact code: topic words ['zzzzz','qqqqqq'] return hook-de-anima-07, a record whose targetText, targetConcept, bridge and relevance are all empty. gold-standard-prompt-builder.ts:712-716 then renders it as "**Bridge [hook-de-anima-07]:** Summary Matrix (Aristotle) ↔ ? (Unknown)" followed by "Both authors (Aristotle and Unknown) MUST be cited with direct textual evidence." A mandatory fabrication instruction, on most sections, today.

The `_hooksDerivationDone` claim is confirmed and worse than stated. Grep over src/, tests/ and scripts/ returns exactly the three lines (:56, :342, :351) and no reset. But "no log line" is wrong in a way that matters: icp-orchestrator.ts:364 logs "Bridge activated" and then :368 abandons the backfill silently, so the trace reads as success. And recompile is not the only trigger — `clearJSONLCaches()` clears the index cache without touching the flag, and any caller passing a non-cwd projectRoot thrashes the single-entry path-keyed cache so the fresh parse lands on the second call. When it fires, gold-standard-prompt-builder.ts:712 interpolates with no fallback and the prompt reads "(undefined) ↔ ? (undefined)". TypeScript cannot see this because cross-author-utils.ts:31-33 declares `sourceAuthor: string` as required over data where the key appears zero times.

Two findings the prior audits missed entirely, both in buildCorpusCatalog. It emits a header saying "only suggest from this list" over 117 of the corpus's 578 titles — 635 of 835 ok manifest records have title_raw but no author_raw, so :159-167 never indexes them, which also makes every correct citation of those 461 works fail `isValidAuthorTitlePair`. And :317's `|| 'secondary'` default mislabels 71 of the 117 it does list, including *The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics* and the Greek Kassel and Ross editions, as SECONDARY SCHOLARSHIP.

On the ultimate goal: I measured what actually reaches a prompt. For a well-matched topic it is 5,271 characters out of 656,755 — 0.803% of the index. Six of each ontology node's ten fields are never rendered; tensions ship without their dependencyRelation or conflictRelation; definitions are cut mid-word at 200 chars (37.2% of all definition text unreachable); units are sliced to 5 (2,259 of 4,059 links dropped). The caps are absolute integers, so at 100x volume the emitted context stays the same size and the discard rate goes from ~82% to ~99.8% — the system gets blinder, not slower, and silently. The hard wall arrives earlier than 100x anyway: reasoning.jsonl is 21.5 MB and readFileSync into one JS string throws at Node's 536,870,888-char limit, i.e. ~25x, uncaught at jsonl-loaders.ts:89.

Verdict: the loader/cache layer is a genuine foundation worth ~150 lines of hardening; the ~600-line matching and rendering layer should be replaced, not patched. Every individual bug there has a two-to-six-line fix you could land in an afternoon and still be left carrying 0.8% of the index as untraceable markdown prose — substring containment, fixed caps and string-typed output are the architecture, not the bugs. Two facts make replacement the cheaper option: the bridge feature has never actually worked on this corpus, so there is no behaviour to preserve; and zero test files reference any of these three modules, so nothing depends on it being stable. The only check that exists, scripts/verify-hardening.ts, is in neither CI nor package.json and passes only because its query contains the one German word that happens to sit in a targetConcept.
